impact:
Two tests in app/Modules/TaskRunner/Tests/Commands/TaskShowCommandTest.php die in the factory call, before task:show is ever invoked, so they test nothing:

- 'shows task with very long name' builds `str_repeat('A', 1000)` and hits SQLSTATE[22001] `value too long for type character varying(255)`.
- 'shows task with null name' passes `'name' => null` and hits SQLSTATE[23502] `null value in column "name" ... violates not-null constraint`.

Both describe a `task_runner_tasks` schema dply does not have: `name` is a NOT NULL varchar(255). This is the same class as ISS-016 (ConnectionManagerTest inserting a servers schema dply lacks) — tests inherited from the upstream task-runner package, whose migrations differed.

The fix is a decision, not a mechanical edit. Either (a) the tests should assert the boundary the schema actually enforces — a 255-char name renders, and a longer one is rejected at write time — or (b) `name` should genuinely be nullable/longer, in which case a migration is the change and these tests are correct in advance. Do not "fix" them by trimming to 254 chars and calling it a long-name test; that stops exercising the boundary entirely.

Out of scope for ISS-015, which covered assertions describing the wrong renderer; these fail before any rendering happens.
title: TaskShowCommandTest creates tasks the task_runner_tasks schema rejects (null name, 1000-char name)
